item.question: The cost of some grocery items is given in the following table. Find the total cost of each item. Rice: 12 kg 500 g, cost of 1 kg ₹60. Flour: 7 kg 250 g, ₹40. Sugar: 5 kg, ₹45. Chana dal: 3 kg 600 g, ₹70. Besan: 4 kg, ₹60. Jaggery: 1 kg 400 g, ₹50.
steps_tex: The total cost is the cost of $1\text{ kg}$ times the weight. Split each weight into whole kilograms and a part of a kilogram.
Flour, $7\text{ kg}\; 250\text{ g}$ at ₹$40$: $7 \times 40 =$ ₹$280$. $250\text{ g}$ is a quarter of $1,000\text{ g}$, so it costs $40 \div 4 =$ ₹$10$. $280 + 10 =$ ₹$290$.
Sugar, $5\text{ kg}$ at ₹$45$: $5 \times 45 =$ ₹$225$.

Chana dal, $3\text{ kg}\; 600\text{ g}$ at ₹$70$: $3 \times 70 =$ ₹$210$. $100\text{ g}$ is a tenth of $1,000\text{ g}$, so $100\text{ g}$ costs $70 \div 10 =$ ₹$7$ and $600\text{ g}$ costs $6 \times 7 =$ ₹$42$. $210 + 42 =$ ₹$252$.
Besan, $4\text{ kg}$ at ₹$60$: $4 \times 60 =$ ₹$240$.
Check: ₹$750$ for the rice is more than $12\text{ kg}$ at ₹$720$ and less than $13\text{ kg}$ at $13 \times 60 =$ ₹$780$.
item.answer_tex: Rice: ₹$750$; Flour: ₹$290$; Sugar: ₹$225$; Chana dal: ₹$252$; Besan: ₹$240$; Jaggery: ₹$70$
steps: The total cost is the cost of 1 kg times the weight. Split each weight into whole kilograms and a part of a kilogram.
Flour, 7 kg 250 g at ₹40: 7 × 40 = ₹280. 250 g is a quarter of 1,000 g, so it costs 40 ÷ 4 = ₹10. 280 + 10 = ₹290.
Chana dal, 3 kg 600 g at ₹70: 3 × 70 = ₹210. 100 g is a tenth of 1,000 g, so 100 g costs 70 ÷ 10 = ₹7 and 600 g costs 6 × 7 = ₹42. 210 + 42 = ₹252.
Check: ₹750 for the rice is more than 12 kg at ₹720 and less than 13 kg at 13 × 60 = ₹780.
item.answer: Rice: ₹750; Flour: ₹290; Sugar: ₹225; Chana dal: ₹252; Besan: ₹240; Jaggery: ₹70

item.question: A cup of juice holds 200 ml or 200 l? A drum of water holds 200 ml or 200 l? These are practice values.
steps: 1 l is 1,000 ml, so a litre is a big amount and a millilitre is a very small amount.
200 l is 200 × 1,000 = 200,000 ml. A cup cannot hold 200,000 ml, so a cup of juice holds 200 ml.
A drum holds much more than a cup. 200 ml is a small amount, so a drum holds 200 l.
Check: 200 ml is far less than 1 l, and 200 l is far more than 1 l.
item.answer: The cup holds 200 ml and the drum holds 200 l
